summary: Ephemeral port reuse on transit-gateway path causes S3 range-download stalls for model artifacts in private deploy
description:
Issue summary: Customers see intermittent stalls and 0-byte ranges when Redwood agent (private deployment via TGW peering) downloads model shard artifacts using HTTP range requests. Impact: model pulls time out or produce corrupted shards causing model load failures and request 5xx at application layer. Behavior is intermittent and correlates with high ephemeral port churn on the customer's NAT/GW.

Observed impact: - Model download failures cause instance restart loops and failed inferences for a subset of hosts. - Customer-facing error rate spike: ~3-6% of artifact GETs in a 1-hour window.

Initial hypothesis: TCP connections for range GETs are being observed as reused/collided due to ephemeral source port reuse across TGW/NAT translation after the customer's flow-aggregation/port-reuse policy. The remote S3 endpoint sees duplicate 4-tuple tuples, and packets from different flows are being delivered to the wrong socket or dropped by an inline stateful device, causing partial/zero-length range responses.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy Redwood Private agent behind customer TGW with NAT gateway enabled and aggressive ephemeral-port reuse configured on corp firewall.
2) Trigger a model pull for redwood-v1.3 (large shard >1GB) so the agent issues HTTP range requests in parallel.
3) Observe agent logs for repeated Range: bytes=... responses that are 0 bytes or have unexpected Content-Range headers.
4) Simultaneously capture flow logs on TGW/NAT and packet captures on agent host to correlate source port reuse events.
logs: 2026-03-12T09:14:22Z agent: fetching shard part 12 range=1258291200-1677721599 -> HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content Content-Range: bytes 1258291200-1677721599/1677721600 (size mismatch)
2026-03-12T09:14:22Z agent: got 0 bytes for expected 419430400 bytes, retrying (attempt 1)
2026-03-12T09:14:24Z kernel: conntrack: NAT translation reused for src=10.0.4.23:40123 dst=52.216.12.34:443 (reused with existing tuple)
2026-03-12T09:14:25Z s3: response with Content-Range header but content-length 0 returned by edge.
investigation_notes: 03/12 10:00 - Support collected agent logs, TGW flow logs, and asked customer to capture tcpdump on a single problematic host.

03/12 13:45 - Packet capture shows two different internal hosts using the same source port to the same S3 IP within < 200ms after customer's NAT port recycling window; server returned 206 for one 4-tuple but packets were delivered to socket belonging to the other flow.

03/13 09:30 - Reproduced in staging by configuring iptables SNAT with aggressive port reuse using ephemeral-port-range <50000 and reuse settings; range requests interleaved and produced occasional zero-length responses.

03/13 11:20 - Hypothesis refined: stateful middlebox (customer NGFW or NAT) is performing source-port reuse or asymmetric state mapping across TGW attachments, leading to cross-flow packet delivery or early TCP teardown observed as 0-length body on range responses.

03/14 08:15 - Eng attempted a mitigation: enable connection pinning on the agent's S3 downloader (force single connection per host for concurrent range requests); reduced failure rate to <0.2% locally but not acceptable long-term for throughput.
comments: Marisol Gomez (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reported intermittent model load failures after a rolling restart. Asking for network captures and TGW flow logs.
Acme NetOps (customer) 2026-03-12: Provided TGW flow logs and noted they run a custom NAT appliance that aggressively recycles ephemeral ports to conserve session table.
Ethan Cole (SRE) 2026-03-13: Reproduced locally with iptables SNAT config. Suspect port reuse collision. Posting preliminary packet captures to #support and linking pcap in Confluence.

Priya Shah (Networking Eng) 2026-03-14: Suggested two workarounds: 1) relax NAT ephemeral-port reuse on customer NAT/GW; 2) enable agent-level conservative connection strategy (single pinned connection per remote host for range streams) until customer fixes NAT behavior.
Acme NetOps 2026-03-14: Will test relaxing ephemeral port reuse and provide results by EOD.
root_cause: Stateful NAT/firewall on customer side was configured to aggressively reuse ephemeral source ports across TGW attachments, causing 4-tuple collisions and mis-delivery of TCP segments for concurrent S3 range requests. This manifested as 0-byte or partial range responses at the agent.
resolution: Short-term workaround implemented: agent patch deployed to prod agents for Acme that pins range-download streams to a single connection per host to avoid parallel 4-tuple reuse. Customer agreed to update NAT/GW configuration to increase ephemeral port range and disable aggressive reuse. Long-term: recommend adding agent-side detection of repeated range response size mismatches and automatic backoff to single-connection streaming, and document NAT recommendations in Private deploy runbook.
timeline_summary: 2026-03-12 initial report -> 03-13 repro in staging -> 03-14 agent workaround deployed + customer to change NAT settings. Monitoring shows error rate dropped from ~4% to <0.3% after mitigations.
